note: Three hand-authored personas for the Agile Checklist maturity engine. calculateMaturity(answers) takes the FLAT 57-item answers map directly (form-app.js calls it as calculateMaturity(state.answers), not the whole assessment) - each key t01..t25/s01..s14/p01..p18 is 'yes'|'no'|'not-applicable'|''. Per-section percent is round2(yes/(yes+no)*100) - not-applicable and unanswered items are excluded from both numerator and denominator; band is unanswered (applicableCount 0) / low (<50) / mid (<75) / high (>=75). overallPercent is the unweighted mean of the three section percents, but ONLY when all three sections have a defined percent AND answeredCount (sum of yes+no+not-applicable across all 57 items, i.e. everything except blank '') is >= 30 - otherwise it is null and maturity is 'insufficient-data' regardless of how good the individual section percents look (persona 3 demonstrates this: two sections are 20% and one is 40%, all genuinely low, but the reported maturity is 'insufficient-data', not 'ad-hoc', because only 20 of 57 items were touched). additionalFlags are folded into the result (push order, NOT sorted by priority - F-STAKEHOLDERS-TRUST/high can appear before F-SECTION-IMBALANCE/medium). Flag triggers read specific item ids directly: t08+p12 both 'no' -> F-FINISHED-WORK; s09+s10 both 'no' -> F-EXPERIMENTATION-BLOCKED; t17+t18 both 'no' -> F-LEARNING-STALLED; any of t22/s08/p14 'no' -> F-PSYCHOLOGICAL-SAFETY (a blank/unanswered item does NOT count as 'no' for these checks, only an explicit 'no' does). Regenerate 'expected' with: bin/test-personas agile-checklist --update

personas.name: High-maturity team - every item confirmed
personas.description: All 57 items answered 'yes'. Expect all three sections at 100% (band 'high'), overallPercent 100, maturity 'optimising', three fired rules (R-TEAMS-HIGH, R-STAKEHOLDERS-HIGH, R-PRACTICES-HIGH), and no flags (every flag-triggering item is 'yes', so none of the negative-signal checks fire).

firedRules.description: Teams have strong agile habits — autonomy, learning, and finishing. Preserve psychological safety as the team grows.
Stakeholders trust and support the team. Continue investing in transparency and shared goals.
Operating practices are healthy — quick decisions, finished-work focus, blame-free culture. Keep watching for over-engineering.

personas.name: Mixed maturity - imbalanced sections with four negative-signal flags
personas.description: Non-critical edge case built to exercise the flag logic precisely. Teams 13/25 yes (52%, band mid); stakeholders 6/14 yes (42.86%, band low); practices 16/18 yes (88.89%, band high) - a 46-point spread between the weakest and strongest section. t08 and p12 are both 'no' (finished-work risk); t17 and t18 are both 'no' (learning stalled); t22 is 'no' (psychological safety, alone sufficient to trigger the flag - s08 and p14 are left 'yes'). All 57 items answered (answeredCount 57). Expect overallPercent round2((52+42.857142857142854+88.88888888888889)/3) = 61.25, maturity 'developing', fired rules R-TEAMS-MID / R-STAKEHOLDERS-LOW / R-PRACTICES-HIGH, and five flags in push order: F-STAKEHOLDERS-TRUST (stakeholders <50%), F-SECTION-IMBALANCE (spread 46.03 > 30), F-FINISHED-WORK, F-LEARNING-STALLED, F-PSYCHOLOGICAL-SAFETY. F-TEAMS-AUTONOMY does NOT fire (teams is 52%, not <50%); F-EXPERIMENTATION-BLOCKED does NOT fire (s09 is 'no' but s10 is 'yes', and the rule needs BOTH no); F-INSUFFICIENT-DATA does NOT fire (57 >= 30).

firedRules.description: Team behaviours are uneven. Identify two or three weak items and turn them into named retrospective experiments.
Stakeholder behaviour is the binding constraint. No team can outrun a sponsor who revokes authority and punishes experiments.
Operating practices are healthy — quick decisions, finished-work focus, blame-free culture. Keep watching for over-engineering.

additionalFlags.description: Stakeholders section scored 43% — sponsorship is the binding constraint.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Brief executive sponsors on agile delegation; renegotiate explicit decision rights.

additionalFlags.description: Section spread is 46 percentage points — adoption is uneven across audiences.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Align coaching across teams, stakeholders, and practices so improvements are not undone elsewhere.

additionalFlags.description: Teams wait on others (t08=no) and the organisation values WIP over finished work (p12=no).
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Set explicit WIP limits and prioritise finishing in-flight work over starting new work.

additionalFlags.description: Teams neither seek (t17=no) nor improve (t18=no) skills — long-term capability is decaying.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Schedule recurring learning time and pair people deliberately on unfamiliar work.

additionalFlags.description: Psychological safety is at risk — dissent, sustained authority, or blameless problem-solving is missing.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Address safety before adding rituals or processes; nothing else compounds without it.

personas.name: Barely-started checklist - insufficient data despite three genuinely low sections
personas.description: Critical/highest persona for THIS engine's specific failure mode: only 20 of 57 items answered (10 teams: 2 yes/8 no; 5 stakeholders: 1 yes/4 no; 5 practices: 2 yes/3 no), the rest left blank. Every touched section is genuinely poor (20%, 20%, 40%), yet overallPercent is null and maturity is 'insufficient-data' rather than 'ad-hoc' because answeredCount (20) is below the 30-item reportability floor - demonstrating that the floor gates on TOTAL items touched, not on whether every section already has a defined (if bad) percentage. t08 and p12 are both 'no'; s09 and s10 are both 'no'; t22 is 'no' (s08 and p14 are left blank, not 'no', so they do not additionally contribute to the psychological-safety trigger, but t22 alone is sufficient). Expect firedRules R-TEAMS-LOW / R-STAKEHOLDERS-LOW / R-PRACTICES-LOW (each section's own percent is genuinely <50 even though the composite can't be reported), and seven flags in push order: F-TEAMS-AUTONOMY, F-STAKEHOLDERS-TRUST, F-PRACTICES-DISCIPLINE (all three sections are <50%), F-FINISHED-WORK, F-EXPERIMENTATION-BLOCKED, F-PSYCHOLOGICAL-SAFETY, F-INSUFFICIENT-DATA. F-SECTION-IMBALANCE does NOT fire (max spread is only 20 points, under the 30-point threshold).

firedRules.description: Teams are not yet operating with agile habits. Start with autonomy, finishing work, and dissent-safety; coaching is needed.
Stakeholder behaviour is the binding constraint. No team can outrun a sponsor who revokes authority and punishes experiments.
Operating practices are working against agility. Address finished-over-WIP, quality-over-deadline, and blame culture before adding rituals.

additionalFlags.description: Teams section scored 20% — autonomy and finishing habits are weak.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Run a focused retrospective on autonomy, finishing work, and decision authority.

additionalFlags.description: Stakeholders section scored 20% — sponsorship is the binding constraint.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Brief executive sponsors on agile delegation; renegotiate explicit decision rights.

additionalFlags.description: Practices section scored 40% — operating practices are working against agility.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Address finished-over-WIP, quality-over-deadline, and blame culture as system-level changes.

additionalFlags.description: Teams wait on others (t08=no) and the organisation values WIP over finished work (p12=no).
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Set explicit WIP limits and prioritise finishing in-flight work over starting new work.

additionalFlags.description: Stakeholders neither support experiments (s09=no) nor tolerate failed ones (s10=no).
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Negotiate a formal experiment budget with the sponsor; agree explicitly that some experiments will fail.

additionalFlags.description: Psychological safety is at risk — dissent, sustained authority, or blameless problem-solving is missing.

additionalFlags.description: Only 20 of 57 items answered; the composite maturity is not reportable below 30.
additionalFlags.suggestedAction: Complete more items before relying on the maturity result.
